title: Strings
objective: Build and transform text with template literals, concatenation, and string methods.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A string is text wrapped in quotes. Single quotes and double quotes both work the same way — pick one style and stay consistent. You can join strings together with the + operator, called concatenation, but you have to add spaces yourself.

Backticks create a template literal, which lets you drop a variable directly into the middle of a string with ${}. `Hello, ${name}!` inserts whatever name currently holds, without any + signs at all — this is the normal way to build a message out of pieces in JavaScript.

Strings come with built-in methods you call with a dot: name.toUpperCase() returns an all-caps copy, name.toLowerCase() returns a lowercase copy, and name.trim() removes whitespace from both ends. None of these change the original string — they return a new one.
explanation.rule: Use a template literal — `text ${variable} more text` — to build a string out of pieces; it's clearer than chaining + concatenation.

examples.title: Template Literals
examples.note: ${smith} and ${swords} are replaced with their values automatically, including converting the number to text.

examples.title: String Methods
examples.note: trim() removes the surrounding spaces first, then toUpperCase() capitalizes the result — neither changes raw itself.

checks.question: What does name.toUpperCase() do to the variable name itself?
options: Returns a new uppercase string; name is unchanged unless reassigned.
Throws an error unless name is already uppercase.

feedback.correct: Correct — string methods return a new string instead of modifying the original.
feedback.incorrect: String methods don't change the string in place — they hand back a new one.

assignment.title: Forge Banner
assignment.brief: Write forgeBanner(smithName) that logs the smith's name in uppercase, followed by the exact text ' FORGE', using a template literal.
requirements: Convert smithName to uppercase using a string method.
Use a template literal to build the final message, ending in the exact text ' FORGE'.

hints: smithName.toUpperCase() gives you an uppercase copy of the name.
A template literal looks like `${smithName.toUpperCase()} FORGE` — the expression inside ${} runs first.
Store the combined string in a variable, then log that variable.
The final output for 'ada' should read exactly: ADA FORGE
